description: Proofs about implications, contradiction and the contrapositive

puzzles.title: \text{Prove: if } n^2 \text{ is even, then } n \text{ is even}
puzzles.displayTitle: Prove: if n² is even, then n is even
puzzles.statement: \text{For every integer } n \text{, if } n^2 \text{ is even then } n \text{ is even.}

blocks.latex: \text{We prove the contrapositive: if } n \text{ is odd, then } n^2 \text{ is odd.}
\text{This is enough, because } p \to q \text{ is logically equivalent to } \neg q \to {{logic:\neg}} p.
\text{Assume } n \text{ is odd, so } n = 2k + 1 \text{ for some integer } k.
\text{Since } 2k^2 + 2k \text{ is an integer, } n^2 \text{ is odd.}
\text{So } n \text{ odd implies } n^2 \text{ odd, and by the contrapositive, } n^2 \text{ even implies } n \text{ even.}

puzzles.title: \text{Prove modus tollens: from } p \to q \text{ and } \neg q \text{, conclude } \neg p

blocks.latex: \text{Assume } p \to q \text{ and } \neg q \text{ are both true, so } q \text{ is false.}
\text{Suppose, for contradiction, that } p \text{ is true.}
\text{From } p \text{ and } p \to q \text{, modus ponens gives } q.
\text{So } q {{logic:\land}} \neg q \text{ holds, which is a contradiction.}
\text{Therefore the assumption that } p \text{ is true is false.}
\text{Hence } {{logic:\neg}} p \text{, as required.}
\text{Suppose, for contradiction, that } \sqrt{2} \text{ is rational.}
\text{Then } \sqrt{2} = \tfrac{a}{b} \text{ for integers } a, b \text{ with } b \ne 0 \text{ and the fraction in lowest terms, so } a \text{ and } b \text{ have no common factor.}
\text{Squaring both sides gives } 2 = \tfrac{a^2}{b^2} \text{, so } a^2 {{op:=}} 2b^2.
\text{So } a^2 \text{ is even, and therefore } a \text{ is even (if } n^2 \text{ is even, then } n \text{ is even).}
\text{Write } a = 2k \text{ for some integer } k.
\text{Substituting: } (2k)^2 = 2b^2 \text{, so } 4k^2 = 2b^2 \text{ and } b^2 = 2k^2.
\text{So } b^2 \text{ is even, and therefore } b \text{ is even.}
\text{Then } a \text{ and } b \text{ are both even, so 2 is a common factor.}
\text{This contradicts the fraction being in lowest terms.}
\text{Therefore } \sqrt{2} {{setop:\notin}} \mathbb{Q} \text{, so } \sqrt{2} \text{ is irrational.}
